stories.headline: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong gets 10 more years in prison
body: A Hong Kong court gave Joshua Wong 10 more years under the national security law.
He was already in prison and had been due for release in January.
The court found he colluded with foreign forces; critics call it part of a crackdown.
stories.vc: Political risk in Hong Kong weighs on its role as a global finance hub.

stories.headline: Arab-led parties back Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
body: The Joint List says it will recommend Gadi Eisenkot to form Israel's government.
With Ra'am's support too, Eisenkot is expected to have 67 backers, above the 61 needed.
Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats.
stories.joke: Kingmakers, with a record seat count.
stories.vc: A new government could reset Israel's budget and foreign policy.

stories.headline: South Africa's ANC heads for new lows in local elections
body: Early results give the ANC about 32% in municipal elections, with the DA on 25%.
Zuma's MK party is third at 8.5%.
Turnout rose to about 54.5%.
stories.joke: The ANC is learning coalition maths the hard way.
stories.vc: Weaker ANC control of big cities like Johannesburg could change how they are run and financed.

stories.headline: Moneyview's profit jumps 5x to ₹201 crore
body: Lending app Moneyview's quarterly profit rose 418% to ₹200.7 crore.
Revenue grew 41% to ₹1,120 crore while costs grew more slowly.
Its shares closed 5.7% higher.
stories.vc: Profitable digital lenders improve the case for fintech listings in India.

stories.headline: Daksham Capital launches a ₹300 crore consumer fund
body: Daksham Capital launched its first consumer fund, targeting ₹150 crore plus a ₹150 crore option.
It closed about ₹125 crore in its first round.
It plans to put ₹5-20 crore each into 10-15 proven consumer brands.
stories.vc: More funds backing proven D2C brands means easier growth capital for Indian consumer startups.

stories.headline: Meta warns voter backlash could slow AI data centre building
body: Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick said the midterm results will make data centres harder to build.
She said the industry has not explained their benefits well.
Opposition to data centres was on the ballot in many places.
stories.joke: Everyone wants AI; nobody wants the building next door.
stories.vc: Local pushback could raise costs and delays for the AI build-out, a risk for chip and power investors.

stories.headline: Democrats will have 100 women in the US House for the first time
body: At least 100 Democratic women are expected to serve in the House at the same time, a first.
Democrats are projected to win back the chamber.
The Democratic Women's Caucus called it historic.
stories.vc: More women in Congress may shift spending priorities towards childcare and affordability.

stories.headline: Latina voters turned away from Republicans in the midterms
body: Latina voters moved away from Republicans in large numbers in this week's midterms, The 19th reports.
Voters cited unsolved money problems and immigration raids.
Their swing helped decide races from Texas to Michigan.
stories.vc: Swing voters focused on prices signal what both parties must deliver on the economy.
